name: Research-process lessons from 16 rounds (what not to repeat)
one_line: Next-bar execution, costs, selection bias, concentration, period-split, bfill/shift look-ahead, stop/TP usually hurt.

source.license: no LICENSE file in repo; owner's own repository (owner-provided reference, do not redistribute)

idea: Collected failure modes from the owner's research log that a new hypothesis should anticipate.
evidence: 1) Look-ahead found twice: fractal signals labelled at bar i but known at i+2; bfill() of fractal lows. 2) Gross-vs-net: 0.04% gross numbers drop to 17.8-20% after 0.10% fees + funding. 3) Best in-sample variants collapsed out of sample (alpha search 5,953 variants: IS Calmar 2.5-3.3 -> OOS -0.5..0.3). 4) Stop-loss, take-profit, ATR stop and account circuit-breakers cut the profit tail and lowered CAGR in the owner's tests. 5) Profit concentration: top-10 trades can exceed 100% of profit. 6) Survivorship bias: coin list = currently alive symbols. 7) Period-definition mixing produced a false pass (Donchian55). 8) Multiple-testing: 239 combos make best-of selection weak evidence.
limitations: owner-written conclusions, not independently re-run here

pipeline_fit.notes: Prefer few fixed a-priori parameters; state each stop/exit as a separate rule so ablation can show whether it matters.
